subject: Television & Streaming
title: When News Came Home
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: When News Came Home.

hook.text: Before TV, Americans read about news in papers or heard it on radio. They never saw it happen live.

buildup.text: In 1951, Edward R. Murrow launched See It Now, bringing filmed reports into living rooms for the first time.

discovery.text: Murrow used the show to challenge Senator McCarthy on air. Viewers watched a bully exposed in real time.

twist.text: CBS executives feared backlash and pulled advertising. Murrow paid for the show's promotion himself.

climax.text: The broadcast helped turn opinion against McCarthy. A single TV program changed American politics.

punchline.text: Television made the news impossible to ignore.

quiz.question: What did Edward R. Murrow's See It Now accomplish?
options: Helped expose Senator McCarthy on live television
